answer: Weight each agent's influence by the square root of its on-ledger committed stake, not by how many keys it controls. One honest agent locking stake S earns about sqrt(S) of pull, a single clear crystal face. A Sybil sharding that same S across 1000 clones nets 1000*sqrt(S/1000) = sqrt(1000)*sqrt(S), only ~32x one honest unit, never 1000x; its payoff curve spirals inward into sharp diminishing returns. Doubling genuine influence demands quadrupling locked capital, so fragmenting into cheap identities offers no haven: reaching Kx pull costs K-squared the real stake.
